key_insight: Turing Agent coordinates theorem and proof formalization to turn research-level mathematical arguments into machine-verified knowledge.
engineering_relevance: Its specialized verification workflow offers a model for building AI systems that produce checkable technical results rather than plausible text alone.
method: Use a two-scale architecture with theorem and proof formalization agents.
Decompose proofs into structured claims and verify them in parallel.
Reuse accumulated proof experience and selectively review semantic fidelity.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports approximately 57–62% faithful formalization success on Formal TCS Bench and 83% overall pass@1 on a TCS-focused RLMEval subset using GLM-5.3 and DeepSeek-V4-Pro.
watch_item: Formal proof acceptance does not alone establish fidelity to the intended theorem; semantic review remains important, and evaluation focuses on theoretical computer science.
paper_title: Turing Agent: Agentic Formal Verification for Mathematical Research
